I have never been to a trail so well marked, with pictures and signs saying what trail goes where.  The trail was really great for us. But with a small amount of dilly dallying, it did take my 11 year old and 1 the full 3 hours to do.  It was amazing to end with a swim and sit on the rock. There was definitely mosquitoes when away from the lake edge. Most of this trail has some view of the lake which was lovely.  I was surprised not to see even one outhouse anywhere (maybe I missed it)  It looked busy, as we parked on the road as the lot was full, but obviously it didn’t seem busy in there. 
There was some up and down hills and rocks in some parts. I didn’t consider it difficult but some would I suppose.  Free to park and enter.

A few bugs and a bit muddy in places but overall great conditions. Amazing views and many spots to get right to the lake.

Lots of fallen tree on the path. But otherwise pretty decent trail. Good length options.

Quite a few downed trees and branches. A few muddy spots. The trail is well marked and great otherwise. Lots of view points and rocks to take a snack break at. The little island and the bridges around it are cool but much shorter than expected.

good trail , long but very pretty!

We followed the advice of others to go in reverse on this trail.  The trail elevated quickly, but what was really challenging is that we decided that to go off the main trail to cut down the length of the trail.  This resulted in a zig zag hike as we had to find our way around the mud and bog.  Not a great idea after all.  There are some very interesting spots. We found the foundation of a house made out of granite with a small wooden structure
10/10 - it’s early season but the conditions were pretty good.  Some parts a bit muddy but nothing you can’t navigate around.  Highly recommend

This is a beautiful trail. Second time I have hiked it - just be aware, going counter clockwise, the second half of this loop has lots of wet boggy areas that need to be navigated around at the moment. I remember this section being muddy in the fall as well but with all the snow melt it’s significantly more worse right now.  Also, as of today, Apr 27, 2025, there are still significant amounts of downed trees and branches from the ice storm blocking and covering the trail which can make route finding a bit more challenging in some areas. Parking is limited and there are no bathrooms or facilities on the trail. I’d say it’s reasonably well marked. The scenery is fantastic. Dog friendly.

We did the hike in a counterclockwise direction. The views this time of year are absolutely gorgeous (the boardwalks were a real highlight) and there were no bugs. I have hiked this trail many times and I always enjoy it. That being said, the conditions were truly HORRIBLE!! The trail seems like it hasn’t been maintained at all. The last 4km, especially, had portions that were either flooded and muddy, layered in snow or so covered in fallen branches it was nearly impossible to see the route. Many times we went off trail without realizing it. Also navigating through all the obstacles extended our hiking time significantly. For those brave enough to try this trail at the moment, waterproof shoes and an early start time (to allow for unintended detours) are a must.
Do the outer trail.  It’s a gem.  Tons of trees across the trail from ice storm.  It can get wet so wear rubber boots.
Recently had a storm so lots of branches/ broken trees on the ground that block the trail. Still easy to get back on track!
Trail is well marked. Boggy at times as still some snow.

The snow on the long loop was insane, we kept falling through it and some points it was up to our thighs when we fell through (hahahah) it was strenuous and added a lot of time due to trail conditions… definitely needs a few weeks to dry up and melt. The fallen branches were also tricky but if you’re up for a challenge - I highly recommend. Otherwise this trail is 10/10!!! Even with the conditions.
Needs more time for the snow to melt. Really poor conditions on the larger loop. Lots of work
Still snow covered for the most part but fairly packed down where people have already walked. Getting soft on the sides though. Beautiful trail!
Deep snow. Snowshoes definitely needed.Amazing hike!
Snowed in. Parking in the side of the road was not an option. No parking signs opposite the park, and snow banks on the park entrance side would put the car more or less into traffic.
Parking lot is snowed in so we had to park on the road. We had to cut the trail for the majority of the hike with snow shoes as no one had been on it since the snow. Challenging but beautiful.
Good trail. Great scenery. Well marked.
Little muddy in some sections, otherwise it was pretty decent. Beautiful trail, love coming here!

Great trail to do! Even if we got caught in some rain for the first half. Second half it stopped raining. Views are incredible with the hike going around the lake. Easy hike with minimal hills there is some. Second half had some mud as well but nothing crazy! No bathrooms available tho. Easy to park but the parking lot is pretty small and fills up fast on a good day. Definitely a trail to do again.

This trail is lovely! There’s some technical aspects that can get tricky so watch your step but it’s such a beautiful loop around the lake! It did work out to just over 10km from the parking lot, but it was worth every step!
Beautiful trail- with some great look out spots. Well taken care of and marked.
Pretty good

Well-marked trail.  Overall, an easy to moderate hike.  We did the full park loop, which included the trail section on the east side of the part.  Although all was nice and dry for us, there could be some wet areas if hiked in rainy times.

The lot and highway near it were crazy jammed with cars which was initially concerning but not many folks at all did the loop A, which is 9 km. Including a half hour swim, about 3 hours. Hike itself can be done in about 2.5 or faster if really moving.
Saw beavers, snapping turtle, water snake. Very pleasant trail for view and water is very clear.

One of my favourite trails. One (1) portable washroom is at the beginning of the trail, not any others. Covered by trees 90% throughout which was great to avoid heat and sun. The lovely breaks where you can swim and relax were awesome, the water was clear and refreshing. Not as crazy bugs but spray yourself regardless as some sections are a bit buggy. Overall love this place!

A little mud won't kill nobody.

Absolutely zero bugs! A bit mucky in some places, but nothing upsetting.

Saw a few people but overall not busy.

Hardy Lake is always beautiful!!! Super muddy in some areas so just be ready for that if you’re coming!
Still very muddy and waterlogged in many areas. Earlier comment from another hiker about big ruts was still true when we hiked. Lots of cool views.

Great trail but someone has ATV'd up in the far West point and made a mess of the path, broke up the packed earth and is all mud for almost kilometer, felt a lot longer. Otherwise one of the better trails we have.

Amazing!

Nice afternoon walk! As others have said is very muddy in parts but that kept it interesting. Had to jump from rock to rock and use fallen logs to cross some streams and swampy bits, I wore waterproof boots and they were definitely needed.
Very muddy in some areas, requires some creative traversing to get around if you aren’t prepared to go straight through. Overall a nice trail with excellent markings.
Definitely can be challenging in parts but great trails. Incredible views walking along the lake. Recommend good boots and pants, muddy in parts but passable

not enough parking space (which is kinda fine), some parts of the trail are flooded, muddy and mucky - had to make a lot of detours through the woods to avoid getting in the water. Great trail.  A few muddy spots. Instead of full loop, modified route since already gave enough blood to the insects.  Well marked and beautiful views.  Will be back for the Fall.
Great day for a swim
Great trail! Every few KM’s it’s as if you are in a different forest! The lake looks like it has so many swim spots for summer. Will be going back!

Absolutely amazing trail, beautiful views,. There are a few spots but you can get lost you got a pay attention to the markers or the trail map. Otherwise very amazing trail I’ll gladly come back here again.￼
Beautiful day, but pretty muddy on some parts. Busy busy trail, so get there as early as possible!
My favorite trail. Beautiful every season. First 1/2 goes inside the forest and the rest along a lake. There are some viewpoints as well where you can sit on warm rock and have a snack if you like

Awesome trail. Very scenic with the trail being beside the lake most of the way. Well marked too. Nice bridges. I could definitely see people coming here to hike and swim! Unfortunately it was a bit too cold for that today but would definitely come back. A bit muddy but we expected this.

very scenic, no lookout points, but overall very beautiful and most of the trail runs along the water. ￼￼￼ there was quite a bit of water and mud in parts, also terrain was rugged so make sure you’re wearing hiking boots that are waterproof. ￼￼
Trails in awesome shape! Now time for a hardy meal
Great trail with lots of scenic views of the lake. In spots, the trail is poorly marked. Follow All Trails map. It’s also a bit muddy in spots.
nice walk

Lovely shortish trail.  Varied terrain mostly along the coastline of Hardy Lake.  You can see some beaver dams from the trail. A little muddy but you could generally navigate around it without issue. Our dog loved it.
Clearly marked. Good solid hike. Nice lake views. Muddy parts especially in the north east corner
Pretty muddy and wet today but overall good! Only saw two other hikers.
Muddy at times but it’s very fun especially if you have the proper shoes and trekking poles!
muddy, bit fun trail.
It’s a lovely trail but quite icy and muddy at times. We enjoyed the hike and peace and quiet it offered :)

This is a mostly gentle hike along a beautiful serene lake. The last 25% of the hike is through some pretty muddy territory and it also has some decent elevation changes. Also lots of log crossings! We started around 12.30 pm when it was not too busy, but it got much busier later in the day. Would recommend!!
a little muddy with some ice in areas. will be clear soon if the weather keeps up. beautiful spots to look over the lake. nice trail to do a picnic
Great trail, a bit icy and muddy in patches but beautiful views and well signposted
It was a lovely walk Muddy in spots that resulted in a little off trail detour. Kids enjoyed the huge boulders and creepy house on the route.
A beautiful hike! The trail is well-marked and moderately trafficked. Watch out for all the mud!
Excellent views, moderate to difficult terrain

March 30th Some ice patches and muddy but totally doable. The river at the top loop is high but still possible to cross hoping on rocks. Easy to follow the trial, signs at every intersections. Beautiful trail as always!
Very icy
Excellent
was a great trail to hike. make sure your phone is charged up as all alltrails takes up a lot of power. phone died while doing the full loop. but the trail is beautiful.
Beautiful scenery!
Trail was packed down snow, not too slippery
Beautiful trail, great look outs over the lake. Well marked. Lightly travelled.
scenic and beautiful trail. heavy snow cover makes it a challenging hike despite its overall distance. Will absolutely be back
I loved this trail!! Dense forests. A neat foundation with small cabin from days gone by. I will definitely return to this one!
It’s great! Make sure to wear proper footwear - quite slippy in some areas.
Yesterday January 9th the trail was really nice. Icy at times but nothing major. 3 or 4 different option depending on how far or long you want to go. Definitely recommend.
Hiked with small kids taking 6km option and absolutely enjoyed every second.
Beautiful trail! Icy in some spots but not too bad overall
Beautiful trail, great in the winter, paths are still clear and lots of options for length! Bridges can get pretty icy but otherwise very nice
Great trail! No mud, beautiful day!
Lake was super muddy (given the snow/rain)  definitely should go wearing appropriate apparel and footwear during this time of year. Still enjoyed though
was a great hike with the family! some muddy areas but was enjoyable.
Snowy and some parts muddy, but overall amazing. Trail markers are white so hard to see in the snow so keep your app handy

This trail is beautiful, lots of wet muddy sections, some with significant water.  lots of puzzle solving to cross some areas with the least likely chance of wet feet.  very grateful it's well marked we had to finish the last 4km with a flash light as we ran out of daylight.  Happens when photographers go hiking we are slower.
Quite muddy/puddly but maneuverable. Well worn and marked. Great Lake views mainly of east side of the loop. Will return to complete with the additional loops (approx 6+ kms).
Great hike! Beautiful lake views, canopy trees, lots of different scenery and terrain. Quite muddy, but doable in hiking boots of waterproof trail runners.
Beautiful trail! Lots of varied terrain. Sort of busy but we went on a sunny Saturday. Very muddy in some spots.
Temperature dropping.  Cold north wind.  Nice lunch spot overlooking a beaver pond.  Would like to come back and hike the entire lake loop.
great hike took us about 4 hrs. muddy in a bunch of areas but super fun. easy to navigate not to busy. moderate hike worth the drive

This was a very nice trail with well marked paths.  currently as if November 8th there are some patchy areas that a bit slick due to wet grounds.  Highly recommend wearing some good boots at this time of year.  walking g sticks aren't necessary if your agile and in good shape. 

Bring a camera as there are some great opportunities.

Great trail! Muddy areas and unfortunately all the leaves are down now. Did the 8.7kms and it took us 4.5 hours with a pit stop to refuel. Weather was lovely as well. I don’t find it too challenging yet great leg workout!

The leaves covered a lot of the trail so it was hard to find the path and the markers were not that clear to see along the west side of the trail. just that time of the year I guess, but over all a nice easy trail.
Beautiful trail! Some muddy and wet spots but overall great. I find it very well marked. Some spots you need to stop and stare at the trees to find the white blaze but easy to figure out.
Fantastic trail. Great scenery and reasonably challenging if you keep the pace up. A bit muddy in certain areas; recommend wearing hiking boots to stay dry.

Very muddy around the back of the lake with all the rain this week, wear hiking boots. A few spots there are side trails so it was handy to have the map accessible. We did the 8km loop, arrived at 10am Saturday, by the time we left around noon it was packed with cars lining both sides of the hwy.
Beautiful for a hike! Go earlier if you want it quieter
Beautiful and peaceful. This has been my favourite place this year, I’ve gone 3 times. Muddy in places but other than that many stunning views
Quite busy (as usual) and muddy (wear boots). Very beautiful this time of year. Took just over 2 hours with minimal stops.
Beautiful. Come early. Beat the crowd
A little bit wet in the low spots but in good shape otherwise lots of trail to explore and beautiful views of the lake
One of my favourite trail this year. Did it 4 times over 4 months, and enjoyed swimming in the lake in July and the beautiful fall colours last week. Half way point is stunning.
Beautiful in parts. Especially near the lake. The forest detour is a bit boring, muddy, and hilly. Also ridiculously crowded closer to the entrance - especially after 10am.
Loved this trail. Great scenery. Some muddy points. We arrived around 9am so it wasn't too busy at the beginning but the trail got busy at the end.

Highly recommend.  We have done this twice and each time the hike has been amazing.  The 9k loop is scenic at every turn. It’s a little muddy in the low lying areas now  but the colours are amazing and we saw one other group. We arrived at the parking lot at 8:15 am.

went Oct 6. most of the fall leaves are on the ground now unfortunately. it was a nice moderate loop, ended up being around 10k including to and from the parking lot. can be muddy in some areas. overall great experience!

Beautiful trail. It had rained the day before, but still only moderately muddy… Nothing impassable. ￼beautiful views of the lake but the landscape remained virtually the same throughout, so not much variety. very dog friendly for my big dog, who has a slight limp. ￼￼
Not the best for fall colours since there is a lot of pine trees. Gets quite busy on the weekend and hard to find parking. Muddy in some places as well. Water is absolutely beautiful and very clean.

Name of hike: Hardy Lake Loop Trail
Length: 8.4 Km
Elevation gain: 218M
Time: 2:28
Hike Type: Loop
Rating: Leisurely 
Parking is on either side of road, trail well marked with white blazes, gentle woodland walk around lake, very pretty views. Although it was Sunday and there were many cars parked on the road, the trail was not crowded.
Finished 8km trails today (last week of September), 20% leaves turning red. Left part of the trail is normal. A few spots in the middle of the trail have beautiful views.
Lovely outlook points throughout the hike.
Gorgeous Fall scenery! Planning on going back sometime soon, hopefully more colourful by then

One of my favorites.  Stunning trail, stunning views and a few different loops depending on how much time you have. just finished the large loop today, so beautiful this time of year. highly recommended

The long trail is a beautiful hike, if you want to take any time to look at the beautiful lake, scenery and pioneer home then I would allocate 3hrs. It has decent ups and downs along with roots and rocks so I would recommend hiking shoes/boots over running shoes. We went in mid September, beautiful weather with a slight breeze.
Great hike on a beautiful day.

Loved this trail. Some excellent viewpoints. The trail is well marked, though we did still manage to take a couple of ‘scenic detours’. It’s up and down, a few muddy spots. Can’t wait to return in a couple weeks to see the fall colours.
Great trail, nice views! Perfect hiking trail.

Nice trail. Easy walk in the wood but fairly long distance. Trail mostly well marked but sometimes easy to lose trail but also not to hard to find it again. Some nice spots to hangout by the water but nothing exceptional.
One of my favourite trails!  Great scenery and lookouts around the lake. Very well maintained and marked.

It was a really nice walk, kinda muddy but it rained the day before. Not a lot of people so its really nice and you can hear the birds and all of the nature around you. There is also some nice spots to go swimming if you really wanted to.

We visited the trail in early september so the weather was perfect - cool and bugless. the trail itself had a very diverse terrain and the level of difficulty was fairly easy. It also had many opportunities for sightseeing.
Some muddy spots no big deal
Very nice afternoon hiking with family.  Encounter wild animal sound 2times.  Maybe bear?! A bit scary.
My girlfriend and I walked in very late May early June was a great trail well marked, clean, great loop, hugs the lake for the most part.

Beauty trail! Didn’t see much wildlife aside from some frogs and salamanders but the diversity is so surreal! It starts off as an easy trail but does get a little harder. I was extremely busy when we went in but barely seen many people on the actual trail! Added some pictures!
busy trail today

Great trail. Marked pretty well.  Trail was a nice combination of hills, roots, rocks and boardwalks. We had to shorten the full route a little due to fading light. 
Boardwalks were updated and so was some of the signage. Trail was clean and other hikers were respectful.

It was lovely. Under an hour’s drive for me. Parking lot and roadside were packed when I arrived but rain drove some people away. So I had a fairly peaceful hike. It’s great for dogs saw lots of dog walkers
Easy hike nice swimming spots, well marked
Fantastic hike. Keep focused on the markings. It’s so beautiful that I got off the trail a couple of times. Luckily the app knew where I was going!
Awesome trail even in the rain. Muddy parts but nothing too bad. Great lookouts and the long trail hugs the water for most of the hike.
Lovely trail right by the water!
Great trail! Fantastic lookouts, scenic view of the lake. The trail is well marked, bridges were shortly renewed. We saw a variety of wild life. Highly recommended!
the trail was really nice, beautiful weather and very quiet hardly any people there. great place for hiking and to take pictures.
Great trail!  If you go clockwise, the nice rocky swimming spots are at the end.  Not too busy on a Friday afternoon...

we did the full 9 km. no bugs at all. trail all in good condition no wet areas all bridges good. moderate to easy hike not any serious ups or downs but long. many trails cross and markings only fair at times so use all trails and guide book to stay on track. easy to go off.
Planned to do the short trail but we’re enjoying ourselves so much we did the big loop.

We did the 8km hike in reverse and it was great. A picnic lunch about half way along the trail by the water. Beautiful day! We didn't end up swimming but I can see why people go to swim there. Decently marked, veered off a couple times but easily re-found the trail. Overall great spot and fortunately almost no bugs

Great spot for a hike and a swim. can be really busy in the summer on weekends so try to make it thru the weekdays if you can. water is nice and clean for swimming and a number of spots you can stop and relax on the shield.
busy, but beautiful. weekdays are probably better than weekends as their were a lot of people on the trail. as many cars parked in the road as in the parking lot.

Great hike in the woods! Wear lots of bug spray! Muddy, but only after lots of rain and was not unbearable. Nice variety along the way, great views of the lake and places to stop and rest on the rocks. Did the 8km loop starting from the parking lot at the west end, by Camp Crossroads, it was a good route that way. All the bridges were fine to cross, even though the sign at one end says one part is under construction. Lovely day out!

Wonderful long trail! Says the bridges are broken and under repair, but honestly the first bridge which was “ok” was the most unstable one, and the other 2 were newly built and sturdy, just the last one had no railings. Very buggy if you take the longer loop, and quite muddy, but very nice scenery. Didn’t realize we could swim after the hike, as people come just to enjoy the water.

Nice trail and not that far away...  Description pretty much sums it up.  Found the markings to be missing at certain points.. so I'd wonder off trail and have use my maps to get me back.  Nice views and moderately traveled.
great walk some muddy areas some buggy areas about 3 hrs to complete watch for roots ands rocks.lots of great swimming spots.

Signs say the bridge is out and you can’t do a full loop. Not true. New bridges are there and I did the full 8.7km loop today. Thanks to the signs, few others were sighted. First km leading to the loop around the lake is paved, rest isn’t.

One of my favourite places to hike. Well maintained. I had no trouble navigating, on the parking you can take a free map, and all crossings have a sign on a tree with a map that shows where you are now.
Plenty of swimming spots. Trail mostly goes through pine tree forest. 
I was there in July, on a hot day, so there were no mosquitoes.
Loved the trail - very nice but too many mosquitos!!! Watch out

This is my first trail, so I cannot compare with others.

I made 8km loop.

As other commented, there were many mosquitos, but with the repellent (continues spraying) it was okay.

The trail is not perfectly marked, but most of the times you know were to go.

You are surrounded of trees, so sun a heat is not a concern.

There are a few areas that are very “scenic” where you can rest and enjoy
Excellent trail a few muddy areas make sure you wear appropriate foot attire. Great trail to spot wildlife also lots of  lovely spots to take a dip

Nice trail but wouldn’t recommend doing the whole loop. Was very muddy in lots of areas & not that scenic on the left side of the lake. 
Could use better signage, did go off for a while & glad I have AllTrails & data. Several areas of rock outcrops to sit or go for a swim on the shorter loops area which also have nicer views

I did the full trail around the lake, not including the outer loop. It took over 3 hours to complete, which was longer than I expected 
Parts of the trail are very well marked, other areas I wanted more markers. 
There are still lots of large muddy areas along the trails where you need to balance across fallen branches & rocks that someone has placed to get across
Come prepared for bugs, there are areas as you get away from the lakeside where they are swarming. 
All of it was well worth it. Beautiful views of the lake, and lots of wildlife. I went mid-week and only saw 3 people - so it’s great if you like to be alone with your thoughts. .
Perfect running trail! Went with my dog on a leash. Would go again.

Don't be persuaded not to do this trail. its was easily marked and there are many flat rocks along the shoreline -  perfect for a beautiful view of the lake for lunch. My advice is  to start left of the trail since there are some muddy spots, and mosquitoes are inevitable, but the opposite side of the trail near the lake had a beautiful breeze. The whole loop is about 3.5 hours, but this goes quick. the water was refreshing for a dip. I would highly recommend since it doesn't cost anything to park, and the trail is fairly flat and enjoyable.

fantastic trail, perfect on a warm day. there are quite a few bugs so be prepared for that. Some muddy spots to wade through but if you've got good shoes on it won't be a problem.  Construction is complete, sign at trailhead re. closures is incorrect. You can do the full loop.

This trail is not maintained, you will have to cross some very muddy areas, fallen trees, unstable bridge. And to add there’s TON of mosquitoes. Couple of views are nice, but I would not recommend this experience.

This trail started off fine but after a couple of kilometres in, the trails became muddy and overgrown. A fallen tree has fallen over at some point, making it nearly impossible to cross over that part to the trail with the amount of branches that are scattered on the ground. Mosquitoes are terrible, making it hard to enjoy the hike.
Very nice.  Some mosquitoes to be expected and some muddy spots, but overall great hike.  Full loop came in at 10k.  Great Lake views.  Very Muskoka!
Pretty trial in all seasons, can be a little muddy at times but overall very nice!
Great trail, bugs and muddy spots on the back half of the trail.

Nice trail, suggest doing it backwards (go left) At the beginning of the trail there were lots of bugs and muddy patches so make sure you have your bug spray and cover up. We followed the lake side trail and it was great. Not many bugs and the breeze was nice. Dog loved it too.
Amazing trail! Bring a bathing suit & towel for swimming in the summer!

My girlfriend and I have walked many trails in Michigan, Quebec and Ontario. Very scenic trails lots of beauty easy to walk a little tricky with marking nothing crazy. Down side was mosquito but that is expected at this of year. The trail is fantastic !!
Lovely hike! Few small sections of mud but totally worth it!
Good view but a bit muddy.

This trail is beautiful, and pretty easy terrain. Only downside to going at this time of year is the mosquitoes are HORRENDOUS. Lots of great spots to stop and swim on a hot day. I would highly recommend bringing a mosquitoe net or at the very least cover your head.

Great trail! Parts of the longer loop had some very muddy/wet spots. Be prepared to either try to figure out how to get around it or get wet. One spot is a relatively deep (enough to get up to your shins wet) stream of water with no real area to cross easily. Otherwise super nice trail with beautiful views of the lake. Definitely recommended
Many patches of this trail are covered in glare ice. Proceed with caution if bringing young children, or others with poor balance.
Well marked and travelled trail. Can’t wait to come back in the summer.
Altered the route by taking the lake instead of the boring inland section. Very wintery day!

Hiked on 29Dec. The eastern and southern side of the lake is fairly icy in places, ice cleats help! Some parts of the small loop were almost impassable. As others have said, a bridge about 2km west of the parking lot is down but passable. Otherwise, a really beautiful trail with some great views of the lake and also Lake Muskoka in the far north of the loop.
Nice easy trail. Fairly busy on the weekend.
One of my favourite trails! I find it the most enjoyable in the winter months when it’s less busy and the hilly terrain keeps you warm on those super chilly days.
Very nice trial , nice views on the way and marked very well!

I did the 8km trail - I started at the end (by the big sign entrance) and I'm glad I did. 2-3km in there's a bit of what I'd say is a boring spot away from the water so I was happy to get that over with . You also avoid going up a steep hill afterwards by going backwards. 
Didn't see any people on the 8km trail but once it met up with the 3km trails I saw quite a bit of people. 
Very easy to follow trail, many markings. Easy walking, too. Dog-friendly.

Really nice trail! Fairly easy with a lot of nice views along the way.
Sign early on had indicated the full loop was not possible as a bridge was out, but I went ahead anyway. The bridge was still intact, but one section had been closed off, although some long, strong boards were put in place of the damaged section. I was able to traverse the short damaged section with no problem at all, and in the worst case, it was not a dangerous situation at all.
Trail is mostly very well marked with maps of the full trail and indications of where you were about every km. or less. Regular white blazers on trees also showed the route, and where another path went in a different direction, there would be 2 uneven blazers indicating a change of direction, similar to the Bruce Trail. However, there were a few spots where it was not marked so well. I did go off course 1 or 2 times, but only for a short distance. When I didn't see blazers for 20 or more m., I would check the AllTrails map, zoom in for accuracy and see I was off the path.
I was there the Tuesday after the Thanksgiving weekend, and it was busier than what I had expected. However, most people hike the shorter loop, so fortunately I did have plenty of peace and quiet. Lots of chipmunks and red squirrels, so bring your nuts along, and also pack a lunch and enjoy sitting by the lake!
Did this trail yesterday on lovely fall day. Lake, fall colours beautiful. Not difficult.
Good trails and well marked. Nice combination of shoreline and forest.
Great trail! However, janky bridge (passable but definitely janky) also, remember bug spray. The bugs are no joke! Good luck. Bring a backup blood supply.

I did the full 8k loop. It was the Sunday of a long weekend so the area is busy but the longer loop still provided long periods of not running into anyone.  Nice, varied terrain. Amazing glacial erratics.
the short loop is better.
great Hiking, make sure you have plenty of bug repellents.

The trail actually came in at 11km on my fit bit. It was buggy but I just kept reapplying deep woods. There are some boggy places where you have to walk over logs but not too bad. This is a great hike...moderate. I had the whole path to myself. I saw no one!

only downfall: bugs, which can't be helped ! 
great 2 hours. minimal bridge damage. no delay/issue at all. so worth it !

Great rugged trail with beautiful scenery. We did the full 8 km loop and didn’t find any issues with construction besides some of the bridge planks missing. We passed a few different people along the way, and so we all made it over the bridge. Lots of boggy, muddy patches you’ll have to cross over though. Fortunately, the breeze from the lake kept the bugs away from us today. Overall, a nice hiking trail in the area. We enjoy hiking and keep a faster pace than most; and this trail took us 2.5 hours to complete. Definitely moderate and experienced hikers should do this trail, and beginners if you are looking for a challenge!
Scenic

An awesome hiking trail around the lake. Clean and well maintained. Moderately trafficked with lots of other dogs. No motorized vehicles on the trail, just foot hiking. A few bridge crossings along the way. (Some of the far out ones about half way are rotting and a bit difficult to cross with a dog.) Made for a very enjoyable afternoon.
Loop not possible due to construction on a bridge at the far side of the lake. Have to turn back. August 2018. Do short loop instead.
It was a little rainy on the day I went.  Ended up being a nice quiet walk under an umbrella.
Enjoyed this hike. Pay attention to the white spray paint marks on the trees. If not for those u would get lost. Nice moderate ability trail. Beautiful lake views.
Great trail with beautiful views
loved it...

A perfect Canadian Shield fix for those looking for rocks, pine trees and water.  There are many scenic views of both forest and the lake. I did the trail a few times winter 2018 in the morning and had no other hikers - lovely solitude. However, I am guessing it is very popular and busy in warmer weather.
Lovely forest, great views along the lake. Nice picnic spots along the water.
Really fun, dynamic hike over rugged ground. Well marked and nice views of the lake. Mosquitoes are very bad so bring some strong repellant.
8.9km walk is actually 12.1kms. Not a complaint, just an observation.
